Statements: Some branches are deposits. All deposits are cards. No cards is a coins.
Conclusions:
I. Some branches are cards.
II. Some deposits are coins.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.stem:

Conclusions:
I. All branches are coins.
II. Some coins are deposits.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.stem:

Conclusions:
I. All branches are coins.
II. No deposits is a coins.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

questions.stem:

Conclusions:
I. Some branches are not deposits.
II. No deposits is a coins.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem:
Statements: P > X < Q = W = V.
Conclusions: I. W < Q   II. X ≥ P.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
rural credit secure = to ni re
rural banking digital = re su ka
credit banking savings = ni su vo
secure digital savings = ka to vo
rural credit savings = vo ni re
What is the code for “savings”?
questions.explanation: Answer: vo. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: rural = re, credit = ni, secure = to, banking = su, digital = ka, savings = vo.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 33 km west, turns left and walks 40 km, then turns left and walks 3 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 50. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 30 km along the initial direction and 40 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(30² + 40²) = 50 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 71 km west, turns right and walks 120 km, then turns right and walks 21 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 130. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 50 km along the initial direction and 120 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(50² + 120²) = 130 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 50 km north, turns left and walks 60 km, then turns left and walks 18 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 68. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 32 km along the initial direction and 60 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(32² + 60²) = 68 km.

questions.stem: C is the mother of E. A is the son of E. D is the father of E. How is A related to D?
questions.explanation: Answer: Grandson. D is a parent of E, and A is E’s son. Hence A is D’s grandchild.

questions.stem: D is the brother of H. H is the mother of G. B is the father of D and H. How is D related to G?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. D is the brother of G’s mother H. Therefore D is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: A is the only daughter of C. C is the father of A. D is the son of A. F is the sister of C. How is C related to D?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. C is the father of A, and A is D’s mother. Thus C is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 53 candidates, a candidate is 21th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 30. New front rank = 21+3 = 24. Back rank = 53 − 24 + 1 = 30.

questions.stem: In a queue of 45 candidates, a candidate is 12th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 30. New front rank = 12+4 = 16. Back rank = 45 − 16 + 1 = 30.

questions.stem: An item costs ₹1750. It is marked above cost and sold at a 20% discount on marked price, earning 25% profit. Find the marked price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 2734.38. Selling price = 1750 × 125/100. Marked price = selling price ÷ 0.8 = 2734.38.

questions.stem: A can finish a job in 30 days and B in 45 days. They work together for 3 days, then B leaves. How many more days does A need?
questions.explanation: Answer: 25. Use 90 work units. Rates: A = 3, B = 2 units/day. Remaining = 90 − 3×5. Divide by A’s rate 3.

questions.stem: A boat travels 153 km downstream and the same distance upstream. Its still-water speed is 13 km/h and stream speed is 4 km/h. Find the total time (hours).
A invests ₹19000 for 12 months. B invests ₹76000 for 4 months. Total profit is ₹98000. Find B’s share (₹).

questions.stem: What is the difference (₹) between compound interest and simple interest on ₹33000 at 20% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually?

questions.stem: A vessel contains 40 litres of milk and water in ratio 3:2. How many litres of pure milk must be added to make the ratio 2:1?
questions.explanation: Answer: 8. Milk = 3V/5, water = 2V/5. Solve (3V/5 + x)/(2V/5) = 2; x = V/5 = 8.

questions.stem: The average of 15 numbers is 58. One number, 70, is replaced and the average rises by 3. What is the new number?
questions.explanation: Answer: 115. Total increases by 15 × 3. New number = 70 + 45.

questions.stem: A father is three times as old as his daughter. After 3 years, their combined age will be 70 years. Find the father’s present age.
questions.explanation: Answer: 48. Let daughter’s age be x. Father is 3x. 4x + 6 = 70; x = 16, so father = 48.
